Obligation trends, FY2026

Source: vignettes/articles/obligation-trends.Rmd
obligation-trends.Rmd

How far below trend are FY2026 obligations to nonprofits? Federal grant and contract obligations to matched nonprofits, October through May of each fiscal year, against the trend set by FY2015–2019 and FY2022–2024. The pandemic-relief years FY2020–21 are shown but not fitted.

Data through Same eight months every yearNominal dollarsDraft · preliminary
Measure

A companion to Nonprofit award disruption, 2025–26 and Disruption on the ledger. Those follow the awards that were already running; this one asks how much new money arrived. The series are built from the full nonprofit database (all transactions to crosswalk UEIs since FY2008) and pre-computed, since that database is not shipped with the package. The measure switch above drives every chart on the page.

The overall trend

Dots: actual October–May totals. Line: fitted trend, dashed where projected. Shaded bands: 80% and 95% prediction intervals for FY2025 and FY2026.

How to read this

  • Window. October 1 – May 31 of each fiscal year. The data run to 6 September 2026 and Defense contract actions post up to 90 days late, so June–September 2026 is incomplete. The months chart below shows how much of a normal year the window covers.
  • Trend. A straight line through the log of each series over FY2015–2019 and FY2022–2024 (a constant growth rate), fitted separately for every group. Series with a zero or negative year are fitted in levels. Eight points make wide intervals; a gap outside the 95% band is a strong signal, one inside the 80% band is not.
  • New awards. Awards whose first action ever (back to FY2008) falls in the window. Contracts under $10,000 lifetime are left out of counts; they are mostly AbilityOne micro-orders. Dollars on new awards is what those awards were obligated in the same window.
  • Population. Recipients are today’s nonprofits matched to USAspending, so earlier years miss organizations that have since closed. Part of the fitted growth is that composition effect, which makes the trend a little steep and the FY2026 gap a little large.
  • Agency is the funding agency on each action (awarding agency where funding is blank); program office is the awarding sub-agency; mission is the recipient’s NTEE major group from the IRS Business Master File.

Share of each fiscal year's obligations by month

FY2023–FY2026. The October–May window holds roughly half a normal year; September alone is often a fifth or more.

Sources

USAspending annual award archives FY2008–FY2026 (generated 2026-09-06) filtered to the npmatch nonprofit crosswalk. Grants (including cooperative agreements) and contracts; loans, direct payments and IDV vehicles excluded. Tables built by pipeline stage 30 (30_obligation_trends.R → trends_tables.json) on .
